chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Yahya ibn Durays al-Bajali (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Maslama al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Lahi'a narrated to us from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from his grandfather,

who said: A man spoke disparagingly of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib in the presence of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, so 'Umar said to him: Do you know who owns this grave? Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib. Do not mention 'Ali except in goodness, for if you disparage him you will hurt this one in his grave.

key_terms.آذَيْتَ: you cause harm or hurt; used here in the sense of spiritual harm caused to the Prophet
key_terms.بِمَحْضَرٍ: in the presence of; denoting a formal or witnessed setting
key_terms.تَنْقُصْهُ: to diminish, disparage, or belittle someone — here referring to speaking ill of 'Ali's rank or virtues
key_terms.وَقَعَ فِي: Arabic idiom for speaking disparagingly or slandering someone; used in hadith to denote verbal abuse or defamation

ai.seo_question: What did 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say when a man spoke ill of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident in which a man insulted 'Ali ibn Abi Talib in front of the second caliph 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. 'Umar rebuked him by pointing out that 'Ali and the Prophet Muhammad share the same noble lineage — both being grandsons of 'Abd al-Muttalib — and that insulting 'Ali would cause harm to the Prophet buried nearby. The incident emphasizes the profound spiritual bond between the Prophet and 'Ali and warns against speaking ill of the Imam.
